The '''45th Academy Awards''' were presented Tuesday, March 27, 1973, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], honoring the best films of 1972. The ceremonies were presided over by [[Carol Burnett]], [[Michael Caine]], [[Charlton Heston]], and [[Rock Hudson]].

The ceremony was marked by [[Marlon Brando]]'s boycott of the Oscars, and his sending of [[Sacheen Littlefeather]] to explain why he could not show up to collect his Best Actor award for ''[[The Godfather]]''; and by [[Charlie Chaplin]]'s only competitive Oscar win, for [[Academy Award for Best Original Score|Best Original Dramatic Score]] for his 20-year-old film ''[[Limelight (1952 film)|Limelight]]'', which was eligible because it did not screen in Los Angeles until 1972.<ref>{{cite news |author=Bruce Russell |agency=[[Reuters]] |title=Cabaret shades Godfather |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=k_dUAAAAIBAJ&sjid=xjwNAAAAIBAJ&pg=3744,6146718 |newspaper=[[Leader-Post]]|location=[[Regina, Saskatchewan|Regina, Sask.]]|date=March 28, 1973 |access-date=June 9, 2013 |quote=The film, withdrawn from U.S. movie theatres in the bitter controversy over Chaplin's political views and private life, qualified by being released for the first time in Los Angeles last year.|via=[[Google News Archive]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Bret Wood |publisher=TCM |url=https://www.tcm.com/this-month/article/29953 |title=Limelight |access-date=June 9, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420051140/http://www.tcm.com/this-month/article.html?isPreview=&id=443505%7C29953&name=Limelight |archive-date=April 20, 2013 }}</ref> Prior to this ceremony, Chaplin had received 2 [[Academy Honorary Award|Academy Honorary Awards]]: in 1972 for his lifetime of work; and in 1929 (after having revoked his nominations for Best Director, Actor, and Writing (Original), thereby presenting him with [[1st Academy Awards#Honorary_Awards|a special award celebrating his multifaceted achievements]]).

With eight wins for ''[[Cabaret (1972 film)|Cabaret]]'', adapted from the [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] stage musical by [[Bob Fosse]], the film set a record for most Oscar prizes without winning [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]]. Best Picture winner ''[[The Godfather]]'' received three Academy Awards.

This year was the first time that two [[Black women|African American women]] received nominations for [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]]: [[Cicely Tyson]] and [[Diana Ross]].<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[Toledo Blade]] |date=February 13, 1973 |access-date=June 16, 2013 |title='Godfather' Gets 11 Oscar Nominations |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=Vc9OAAAAIBAJ&sjid=-AEEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7352,3061459 |author=Bruce Russell |agency=Reuter}}</ref> Minnelli accepted her Oscar despite a slight scrape she had incurred while riding a motorcycle. Ross was criticized for running a promotional ad campaign demanding that she win the Best Actress Oscar.<ref name="Oscars '72 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/846/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=846 |isbn=0-385-04060-1|author-link=David Wallechinsky|author-link2=Irving Wallace}}</ref> Meanwhile, [[Edward G. Robinson]], who died two months before the ceremony, became the second actor to receive his honorary Oscar [[Posthumous award|posthumously]], after [[Douglas Fairbanks]] (d. 1939) in 1940.

This was also the first year when all Oscar winners were brought on stage at the end of the ceremony.<ref>{{YouTube|id=_8PPRhEws-0|title=John Wayne and the Academy Award Winners: 1973 Oscars|link=no}}</ref> The show drew a television audience of {{nowrap|85 million}} viewers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Robinson |first1=Melia |title=The unbelievable story of Why Marlon Brando rejected his 1973 Oscar for 'The Godfather' |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/marlon-brando-rejected-godfather-oscar-2014-2 |access-date=1 June 2020 |work=[[Business Insider]] |date=February 27, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |people=[[Marlon Brando]], [[Dick Cavett]] |date=12 June 1973 |title=Marlon Brando on Rejecting His Oscar for 'The Godfather' |medium=television |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rcCKczj4aK4  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/rcCKczj4aK4 |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|access-date=30 May 2020 |format=video |time=0:49 |work=[[The Dick Cavett Show]] |location=United States}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

* ''[[The Poseidon Adventure (1972 film)|The Poseidon Adventure]]'' – [[L. B. Abbott]] and [[A. D. Flowers]].

=== Honorary Awards ===
* To Charles S. Boren, leader for 38 years of the industry's enlightened labor relations and architect of its policy of non-discrimination. With the respect and affection of all who work in films. 
* To [[Edward G. Robinson]] (†) who achieved greatness as a player, a patron of the arts and a dedicated citizen... in sum, a Renaissance man. From his friends in the industry he loves. (Accepted on his behalf by his wife)

== Eligibility controversies ==
It was initially announced, on February 12, 1973, that ''The Godfather'' received 11 nominations, more than any other film that year.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=Toledo Blade |date=February 13, 1973 |access-date=September 2, 2014 |title='Godfather' Gets 11 Oscar Nominations |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=Vc9OAAAAIBAJ&sjid=-AEEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7352,3061459 |author=Bruce Russell |agency=Reuter}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |newspaper=The Milwaukee Journal |date=February 13, 1973 |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NEkoAAAAIBAJ&sjid=uigEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7519,2024505 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130620052919/http://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NEkoAAAAIBAJ&sjid=uigEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7519,2024505 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 20, 2013 |access-date=June 16, 2013 |title=Oscar Nominations Offer Few Oddities }}</ref> This was reduced to 10 nominations (tied with ''Cabaret'' for the most) after a new vote by the academy's music branch, following a controversy over whether [[Nino Rota]]'s score for ''The Godfather'' was eligible for the nomination it received.<ref name=Godfather>{{cite news |newspaper=The Star-Phoenix |agency=AP |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=4gpgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=828NAAAAIBAJ&pg=985,824836 |date=March 3, 1973 |access-date=June 16, 2013 |title=The Godfather loses one count}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.afi.com/members/catalog/DetailView.aspx?s=&Movie=54023 |access-date=June 16, 2013 |work=AFI Catalog of Feature Films |title=The Godfather |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140717165334/http://www.afi.com/members/catalog/DetailView.aspx?s=&Movie=54023 |archive-date=July 17, 2014 }}</ref> For the re-balloting, members of the music branch chose from six films: ''The Godfather'' and the five films that had been on the shortlist for best original dramatic score but did not get nominated. [[John Addison]]'s score for ''Sleuth'' won this new vote, and thus replaced Rota's score on the official list of nominees.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paramount.com/paramount-academy-awards/tags/143/the-1970s |quote=The Godfather score, composed by Nino Rota, was originally announced as one of the five official nominees. It was later pointed out that portions of the score and the main theme were composed by Rota for his score to the 1958 Italian film, Fortunella. The Music Branch was given this information and re-balloted to determine the fifth nomination. The list of six films they were to choose from were the remaining five of the top ten preliminary listings, plus The Godfather score. The results of the re-balloting was that the fifth nomination became Sleuth, composed by John Addison. |access-date=June 16, 2013 |title=100 Years of Paramount: Academy Awards |publisher=Paramount Pictures |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604233242/http://www.paramount.com/paramount-academy-awards/tags/143/the-1970s |archive-date=June 4, 2013 }}</ref> The controversy arose, according to Academy President Daniel Taradash, because the love theme in ''The Godfather'' had previously been used by Rota in ''[[Fortunella (film)|Fortunella]]'', an Italian movie from 1958.<ref>{{cite news |publisher=The Montreal Gazette |agency=AP |title=Godfather, Superfly music out of Oscars |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=uscuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=f6EFAAAAIBAJ&pg=871,1907982 |date=March 7, 1973 |access-date=June 16, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181121195947/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=uscuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=f6EFAAAAIBAJ&pg=871,1907982 |archive-date=November 21, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> Pacino also did not attend the ceremony; he was allegedly insulted at being nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor, when he had more screen time than his co-star and Best Actor-winner Brando, and thus should have received the nomination for Best Actor.<ref name="Grobel; p. xxi">Grobel; p. xxi</ref> Pacino denies this, saying in his memoir, ''Sonny Boy,'' that he was "scared" of his sudden fame and never heard the rumor until much later in his life.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=Lottie McGrath Freelance News |date=2024-10-26 |title=Al Pacino sets record straight on why he "didn't show up" to Oscars |url=https://www.newsweek.com/al-pacino-oscars-rumor-set-straight-oscars-snub-1975017 |access-date=2024-11-21 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref>

The nominations in the category of Best Original Song were not announced in February with the rest of the nominations, reportedly because of "a mixup in balloting".<ref>{{cite news |access-date=June 16, 2013 |date=February 13, 1973 |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NEkoAAAAIBAJ&sjid=uigEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7519,2024505 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130620052919/http://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NEkoAAAAIBAJ&sjid=uigEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7519,2024505 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 20, 2013 |quote=Because of a mixup in balloting, the nominations for best song won't be announced until March 5. |title=Oscar Nominations Offer Few Oddities |newspaper=The Milwaukee Journal }}</ref> It was later reported that the academy had been considering whether [[Curtis Mayfield]]'s song "[[Freddie's Dead]]" from the film ''[[Super Fly (1972 film)|Super Fly]]'' should be eligible. The song was ruled ineligible for a nomination because its lyrics were not sung in the film. (The song was released as a single with lyrics, but the version in the film was an instrumental.) Academy governor John Green was quoted as saying: "Times have changed. In the old days, Hollywood made 30 or 40 musicals a year, and there were plenty of songs to choose from. Now there are hardly any, and most of the eligible songs are themes. Both the lyric and the music must be heard on the sound track to be eligible."<ref>{{cite news |title='Godfather', 'Super Fly' Music Not Nominated For Oscar |newspaper=The Toledo Blade |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=Ks9OAAAAIBAJ&sjid=-QEEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4356,4776086 |agency=AP |access-date=June 16, 2013 |date=March 7, 1973}}</ref>

== Sacheen Littlefeather's appearance ==
{{see also|Sacheen Littlefeather#1973 Academy Awards speech}}
[[File:Sacheen Littlefeather Oscar 45 (cropped1).jpg|thumb|[[Sacheen Littlefeather]] holding [[Marlon Brando]]'s statement at the 45th Academy Awards]]
[[Sacheen Littlefeather]] was an American actress, model, and activist of [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] civil rights who [[Marlon Brando]] chose to represent him at the ceremony.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marlon Brando |url=http://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000008/awards |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=[[IMDb]]}}</ref> Littlefeather took the stage and spoke on Brando's behalf as a form of protest, representing Native Americans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 13, 2009 |title=Marlon Brando declines Best Actor Oscar |url=https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/marlon-brando-declines-best-actor-oscar |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=HISTORY}}</ref>

The audience in the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion was divided between applause and jeers.<ref name="Rottenberg">{{Cite magazine |last=Rottenberg |first=Josh |date=January 19, 2013 |title=Catching up with Sacheen Littlefeather, 40 years after her controversial brush with Oscar history |url=http://ew.com/article/2013/01/19/sacheen-littlefeather/ |url-status=live |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220421065228/https://ew.com/article/2013/01/19/sacheen-littlefeather/ |archive-date=April 21, 2022 |access-date=April 7, 2018}}</ref> "I was distressed that people should have booed and whistled and stomped, even though perhaps it was directed at myself," Brando later told [[Dick Cavett]]. "They should have at least had the courtesy to listen to her."<ref name="Rottenberg" /> Her appearance prompted the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] to rule out future proxy acceptance of Academy Awards. (Oscars for winners unable, or unwilling, to accept in person are now accepted in their behalf by the presenters.)<ref>{{cite news| title= Oscar Watch; Oscar takes a bow for legacy of controversy| first= Stephen |last= Schaefer| work= Boston Herald| date= March 16, 2003}}</ref>

Both Sacheen Littlefeather and [[Marty Pasetta]], who directed the Academy Awards telecast, claimed that [[John Wayne]] had to be restrained by six security guards to prevent him from assaulting Littlefeather.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ibrahim |first1=Nur |title=Did John Wayne Try To Pull Sacheen Littlefeather Offstage at 1973 Oscars? |url=https://www.snopes.com/news/2022/03/31/john-wayne-sacheen-littlefeather/ |website=Snopes |date=March 31, 2022 |access-date=5 April 2025}}</ref> The story was later refuted as having "never happened" by film historian Farran Nehme. She characterised Pasetta's account as "getting more exciting each time it was told".<ref>[https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2022-08-23/column-did-john-wayne-try-to-assault-sacheen-littlefeather-at-the-1973-oscars-debunking-a-hollywood-myth Did John Wayne try to assault Sacheen Littlefeather at the 1973 Oscars? Debunking a Hollywood myth]</ref>

== Presenters and performers ==
The following individuals, listed in order of appearance, presented awards or performed musical numbers. 

Notably, Charlton Heston was late for his role presenting the voting rules, reportedly due to a flat tire. Clint Eastwood, who was slated to present for Best Picture, was asked to fill in. Heston's written dialogue leaned heavily on his role in the movie ''[[The Ten Commandments (1956 film)|The Ten Commandments]]'', leading Eastwood to quip, "Come on, flip the card, man. This isn't my bag." Eastwood also famously said on filling in at the last minute, "...They pick the guy who hasn't said but three lines in 12 movies to substitute for him [Heston]". Heston arrived part of the way through the bit, allowing Eastwood to escape.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=The Most Memorable Moments in Oscar Hosting History|url=https://time.com/5534588/oscar-hosts-memorable-moments/|magazine=Time|date=February 21, 2019 |language=en|access-date=2020-05-13}}</ref>
